narrative:
The model determined that you have an 84% probability of representing a bad credit risk. This high likelihood led directly to the denial of your loan application.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the length of the loan you requested, and your property ownership situation. 

Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the single biggest reason for the rejection. While only 12.6% of approved applicants have accounts in this state, the majority (59.2%) have no checking account at all. This negative status strongly pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk.

The 60-month duration you requested was the second most important factor. This is more than three times longer than the average 19-month duration among approved applicants, and this extended timeframe also significantly increased your risk score.

Your lack of identifiable property (unknown/none) was the third key driver. This is relatively uncommon, as only 7.8% of approved applicants fall into this category, and it further contributed to the negative assessment.

While some aspects of your profile, such as your long employment history and age of 63, likely worked in your favor, they were not enough to overcome the impact of these three dominant factors.

To improve your chances on future applications, focus first on bringing your checking account into positive territory, consider applying for a shorter-term loan that better matches typical approvals, and gather documentation about any assets or property you may have. These changes would address the main reasons behind this decision.
